title: Tier Sets
content: Vanilla class tier armor gives set bonuses when several pieces are equipped. Tier 1 comes mainly from Molten Core; Tier 2 comes mainly from Blackwing Lair with additional pieces from Onyxia and Ragnaros; the Ahn'Qiraj class sets are commonly called Tier 2.5; and Tier 3 comes from Naxxramas token quests. Turtle WoW also adds custom level-60 sets, so compare bonuses with the intended role rather than assuming a later tier is always best.

title: Legendary Weapons
content: Legendary weapons are the most powerful items in the game, requiring extensive quests and rare materials to obtain. Examples include Sulfuras (Ragnaros), Thunderfury (Thunderaan), and Atiesh (Medivh). These weapons have unique appearances, powerful stats, and often special abilities. Obtaining a legendary weapon is a major accomplishment that requires dedication and coordination with other players.

title: Profession Tools
content: Many recipes require a specific tool or nearby station. Blacksmiths use a Blacksmith Hammer and often an anvil; miners use a Mining Pick and forge; engineers use tools such as a Gyromatic Micro-Adjustor; enchanters need runed rods; and skinning requires a Skinning Knife. Vanilla crafting normally succeeds when requirements are met, so ordinary tools do not raise item quality or success chance unless their tooltip explicitly grants a skill bonus.

title: Mount Collection
content: Vanilla and Turtle WoW offer racial ground mounts plus rarer mounts from reputations, PvP ranks, quests, custom content, and drops such as the Swift Zulian Tiger or Deathcharger's Reins. Standard riding begins at level 40 and epic ground riding at level 60 unless a custom reward says otherwise. There are no level-70 flying mounts or achievement-awarded mounts in the Vanilla ruleset.

title: Weapon and Armor Enchants
content: Enchants add permanent magical bonuses to eligible weapons and armor. In Vanilla, an enchanter normally applies the enchant directly through the trade window rather than creating a sellable enchant scroll. Common choices include Crusader, Fiery Weapon, Agility, weapon damage, attributes, armor, resistances, healing, and spell damage. The later Soulfrost enchant is not part of this ruleset.

title: Crafting Gems and Arcane Crystals
content: Vanilla equipment has no colored sockets, meta gems, or Jewelcrafting profession. Gems such as Citrine, Jade, Aquamarine, Star Ruby, Azerothian Diamond, Blue Sapphire, and Huge Emerald are trade goods used directly in recipes and quests. Rich Thorium Veins can also yield Arcane Crystals, which alchemists transmute into Arcanite Bars for important crafted equipment and legendary quest materials.

title: Consumable Items
content: Consumables are items that provide temporary benefits when used. Food provides stat buffs, potions restore health/mana or provide temporary boosts, elixirs give longer-lasting buffs, flasks provide raid buffs. Alchemists and cooks create many consumables. Using proper consumables before encounters is essential for raid and dungeon performance. Some consumables are very rare and expensive.

title: Trade Goods and Materials
content: Trade goods are materials used in professions. Cloth from humanoids, ore from mining nodes, leather from beasts, herbs from gathering. These materials are bought and sold on the auction house. Prices fluctuate based on demand. Professional players make gold by farming and selling materials. Understanding market values is important for both crafting and trading professions.

title: Dungeon and Raid Keys
content: Keys and attunements open locked routes or instances in Vanilla. Examples include the Shadowforge Key for Blackrock Depths, Skeleton Key for Scholomance, Crescent Key for Dire Maul, Key to the City for Stratholme, Seal of Ascension for Upper Blackrock Spire, Drakefire Amulet for Onyxia's Lair, and the Core Fragment attunement for Molten Core. Rogues can pick some ordinary locks, but raid attunements still require their quest conditions.

title: Special Containers
content: Containers include normal bags, profession-specific bags, lockboxes, quest packages, fishing trunks, clams, and boss or event reward caches. Some require a key, Rogue lockpicking, a quest condition, or enough bag space before opening. Their contents can include coins, reagents, recipes, equipment, or quest items. Read the tooltip before deleting an apparently ordinary container because it may start or complete a quest.

title: Guild and Faction Tabards
content: Tabards occupy the tabard slot and usually display a guild, faction, PvP rank, event, or accomplishment. A guild master can design a guild tabard and members can purchase copies. Most Vanilla tabards are cosmetic and do not grant reputation merely by wearing them, although a particular quest or custom Turtle WoW item may check for one. Read the exact tooltip rather than assuming later expansion tabard behavior.

title: PvP Equipment
content: Vanilla PvP equipment comes from faction ranks, battleground reputation, marks, and honor-system rewards rather than rated arenas. Sets and weapons such as Grand Marshal and High Warlord gear emphasize strong general combat stats, stamina, and set bonuses; the later Resilience and PvP Power stats do not exist. PvE pieces can still be valuable in PvP depending on class, survivability, and burst needs.

title: Quest Reward Items
content: Quest rewards can provide weapons, armor, trinkets, recipes, keys, and class-defining items. Vanilla examples include Verigan's Fist for paladins, the Whirlwind weapon chain for warriors, Rhok'delar and Lok'delar for hunters, and Benediction or Anathema for priests. Compare every reward before completing a quest because choices are often permanent and an unusual utility or resistance item may remain valuable.

title: Cosmetic Items
content: Shirts, tabards, companion pets, mounts, disguises, holiday items, and unusual consumables provide visual flavor. Turtle WoW also includes a custom transmogrification feature when enabled by the server, allowing compatible appearances to be applied under its own costs and restrictions. The Vanilla client has no modern toy-box, appearance collection, or weapon-illusion interface, so many cosmetic objects remain physical inventory items.

title: Relics and Artifacts
content: Relics are class-specific equipment: librams for paladins, idols for druids, and totems for shamans. In this Vanilla ruleset they occupy the ranged/relic equipment slot rather than an off-hand slot and modify particular abilities or stats. Compare the exact effect with the character's role because a rare relic is not automatically best for every talent build.
